title: Add RAG blueprints and minimal agent skeletons quickstart
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Add new RAG quickstart with opinionated blueprints and minimal agent skeletons (TS + Python). Includes example config, prompt sets, and eval integration. Non-breaking; developer-facing docs and examples only.
description: Motivation: path teams frequently ask for a compact, production-minded starting point for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and agent-style tool calling. This PR adds a small, opinionated quickstart that we can point users to from the docs site and onboarding emails. Summary: introduce two language-agnostic blueprints (blueprint/rag-orchestrator.yaml and blueprint/agent-skeleton.md) and two runnable examples (examples/ts-minimal-agent and examples/py-minimal-agent) that demonstrate: 1) wiring a Redwood retrieval index to a RAG orchestrator; 2) a minimal tool-calling agent loop with function metadata and safe fallbacks; 3) prompt-set versioning and an example eval harness integration. Files added are intentionally small and self-contained so they can be cloned and run locally with free credits. What this is NOT: a full-fledged production deployment or performance benchmark. Checklist: - [x] Add blueprints and quickstart README with step-by-step run instructions and environment variables - [x] Provide TypeScript and Python minimal agents with docker-compose for local testing - [x] Wire example prompt sets and a sample eval config referencing eval-harness - [x] Add docs site link and cross-reference to RAG playbooks page - [x] Unit tests for the orchestration helper and prompt sanitizers - [x] Smoke CI job to build both examples and run lint/format How to run locally: follow README.quickstart in the new examples folder; both agents support REDWOOD_API_KEY and a local sqlite vector index used only for demo. Security: examples avoid real credentials, include clear KMS notes, and default to sandbox model pins. Related work: follows guidance from ENG-4827 (RAG patterns) and DOC-1034 (quickstart consolidation).

review_comments: Ethan Cole (reviewer): Nice concise quickstart. A couple of notes: prefer explicit model pins in the examples and avoid 'latest' model tags. Please add a short sentence about expected token usage for the demo so users don't blow credits.

Sofia Martinez (author): Good call. I pinned the model in both examples to open-compat/gpt-3.8-small and added an 'expected cost' section in README.quickstart.md. Also added a note about using free credits or local small models for smoke runs.
Priya Raman (reviewer): Can we add a single E2E smoke test that runs the TS example in CI and verifies the agent loop completes one tool call? That will help keep the example healthy as deps change.

Sofia Martinez (author): Added a lightweight smoke job that builds the docker image and runs the ts example with a mocked retriever/tool; it runs under 60s and is gated behind an examples-only workflow. Tests added to CI and green locally.
Lukas Weber (approver): Verified docs link and playground snippets render correctly. Approving — please squash on merge.
